verdict.rationale: CoreWeave's CKS is a managed Kubernetes service running directly on bare metal (no VMs), which implies developers can deploy their own container images as standard Kubernetes workloads, and Node Pools let you define custom hardware/instance configurations. However, the evidence pack never explicitly documents bringing your own Docker image, a container registry integration, or a 'custom machine template' feature — this is only inferred from generic Kubernetes/CKS architecture docs. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of custom image/registry support, VM/instance templating equivalents, and any hands-on confirmation that arbitrary Docker images run as expected on CKS.
